clinician.trajectory_summary: A 22-month-old boy presented with a 3-week history of fever, cough, night sweats, dyspnoea, and chest indrawing, with an initial leukocytosis (TLC 98,000 cells/µl). Chest radiograph revealed heterogeneous opacification in multiple right lung lobes. Physical examination showed pallor, wasting, tachypnoea, crackles on right chest, and hypoxia. Blood cultures were negative. Although a CT chest was ordered, no results were reported. The patient was started on intravenous antibiotics and tuberculosis treatment. Clinical improvement was noted within 3 days of antibiotics initiation, with resolution of fever and respiratory distress and normalization of leukocyte count (TLC 7,670 cells/µl) by discharge at 17 days. No pleural fluid analysis or pathology/biopsy reports were available. This clinical course and imaging findings support the diagnosis of necrotizing pneumonia.
